data.why: the repo already bundles procedural synthetic chickpea images (generated at install time into data/raw/ for diagnosis/benchmarking) plus real multi-view specimen photos pre-staged in data/real_staging/incoming/ for the review workflow, so no external or synthetic data needs to be authored

goals: upload or select a single chickpea seed photo and get a predicted quality grade (sound_healthy, discolored_spotted, broken_cracked, shrivelled_damaged) with a confidence score
inspect a Grad-CAM heatmap and blended overlay to see which seed-coat regions (spots, cracks, wrinkles) drove the model's decision
compare the custom SeedNet-Baseline CNN against the MobileNetV2 transfer-learning model on the same seed image and across benchmark metrics
review incoming real specimen photo batches (multiple angles of the same physical seed) and assign a verified defect label with reviewer notes
check accuracy, macro F1, calibration (ECE), confusion matrices and latency for each architecture on the held-out test split
undo or revert a specimen review decision using the automatic manifest backup if a labeling mistake is made

review.summary: The tree states the tool's purpose exactly: four-class chickpea grading with Grad-CAM, multi-view human label curation with backup and revert, and a two-model benchmark. It covers every goal in plan.json at the right depth with faithful labels, and all ten screens I opened support their nodes. The gaps are minor (defect-class Grad-CAM was blocked by an app quirk, plus the Home page and some duplication), so it can be filed as is, with the optional fixes noted.
